chains.title: C228T creates a de novo ETS site occupied by GABPA (GABP complex), activating TERT in glioblastoma
chains.element: TERT core promoter cCRE EH38E3622530 (PLS), chr5:1294945-1295294

links.claim: 18 ETS-specificity models pass the QBiC gate, all alt-preferring, and the site rises from the 97.1th to the 99.3th percentile of k-mer coefficients; within this shared-specificity group GABPA is chosen because it is the only member with direct occupancy evidence at this exact base (two ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks containing chr5:1295113 in HepG2 and SK-N-SH), has its own passing model (z 68.47) and is expressed at 15.5 TPM in glioblastoma lines; the literature also states that canonical TERT promoter mutations create de novo ETS-family binding sites

The variant lies in an active promoter-like cCRE at the TERT TSS with high DNase, H3K4me3 and H3K27ac (z-scores are maxima across biosamples, not glioblastoma-specific), and VEP annotates a promoter regulatory feature

TERT is 0 kb from the variant and is the only gene whose TSS the cCRE abuts; literature states these promoter mutations promote TERT expression partly by generating novel TF binding sites. Support beyond proximity plus literature is still indirect (no eQTL or isogenic knock-in data here)

GABPA is expressed at 15.5 TPM across 54 glioblastoma lines and the promoter cCRE is in an accessible, active state, so the created site can be occupied; GABPA is a DepMap common essential, so its strong knockout effect in CNS lines is not lineage-specific evidence

Telomerase reactivation averts replicative senescence; TERT promoter mutations are among the most frequent alterations in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma and occur in 50-82% of melanomas. These quotes concern TERT promoter mutations generally, not GABP specifically

Reporter activity gain requires the created ETS core; mutating it abolishes the gain

chains.title: The new ETS-type site is bound by ETV6, whose repressive occupancy modulates rather than drives TERT output

grades_v0.reason: Only QBiC-SELEX predictions (E05/E06) back this: GABPA has its own passing model (z 68.47, alt binds more) and 15.5 TPM. The claim that GABP needs two spaced GGAA sites and is distinct from ETV5/ELF1 is not in any cited evidence. No ChIP, reporter or perturbation data are provided.

E03 places the variant in PLS cCRE EH38E3622530 with high DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 z-scores, and E01 gives a promoter regulatory feature. These are maxima across biosamples and not glioblastoma-specific, which is a minor caveat.
TERT is 0 kb from the TSS (E01/E02), which is proximity only. No eQTL, CRISPR or reporter evidence shows the allele raises TERT. The claim of reactivation from a silenced promoter is not shown.

GABPA expression of 15.5 TPM (E06) and generic cCRE accessibility are consistent with occupancy. Accessibility is a maximum over biosamples, not glioblastoma-specific. No ChIP in glioblastoma lines is shown.

E04a and E04f show TERT promoter mutations are frequent in melanoma and IDH-wt GBM, and E04e links TERT to senescence. None of these quotes ties this variant, or GABP, to the phenotype mechanistically. The quotes do not say C228T specifically.

ETS1 is only CIS-BP-mapped within G003 and is not among the listed passing members. Choosing it for its TPM rather than its own binding evidence is weak. The QBiC result for the group is for a different TF (ETV5) and is applied to ETS1 without a model-specific result.
E03 shows the variant lies in the active promoter-like cCRE.
E02 shows only that TERT is nearby. Nothing shows ETS1 occupancy changes TERT transcription.
ETS1 at 61 TPM (E06) shows it is expressed. The claim that it outcompetes GABP is unsupported by any evidence.
E04a and E04f are generic about TERT promoter mutations and do not mention ETS1.

ETV6 passes in G020 (z 46.32, alt binds more, own model per E07). Choosing it by elimination of low-TPM members is reasoned but rests on prediction only. The claim that ETS sites are repressor-class here is not evidenced.
E03 only shows an active promoter. It says nothing about ETV6 repressing in this context, which is asserted from outside knowledge.

E02 gives distance only. No evidence shows ETV6 dampens TERT. The direction is also inconsistent: alt binds more, so ETV6 repression would predict lower TERT in mutants, against the known gain of expression.
E07 gives 5.65 TPM for ETV6, so it is expressed modestly. There is no glioblastoma occupancy data.
E04c and E04d concern the rs2853669 SNP in cis with the promoter mutation, not ETV6. In that cohort cis status lowered TERT expression, and the quotes do not connect this to ETV6 occupancy.

E09 shows 4 AP-2 models with a negative effect, and TFAP2A has its own model (z -28.06, 9.65 TPM). The prediction is in vitro only. The site loss is consistent in direction (ref binds more) but unvalidated.
E03 shows an active promoter cCRE. It does not show an AP-2 site matters there.
No evidence shows AP-2 represses TERT. The claim is conditional ('if AP-2 acts as a repressor') and E02 only shows proximity.
TFAP2A and TFAP2C are expressed in glioblastoma lines (E09), so occupancy of the ref allele is plausible. No ChIP data are provided.
E04a and E04f are generic about TERT promoter mutations and do not mention AP-2 loss.

grades_final.reason: QBiC predicts alt-preferring ETS binding, GABPA has its own passing model (z 68.47) and ChIP peaks overlap the base, and the literature says canonical mutations create ETS sites. However, the ChIP peaks are in HepG2 and SK-N-SH, not glioblastoma, and are not allele-specific. There is no perturbation evidence. The GABPA choice is reasoned but the evidence is indirect.

The variant lies in a PLS cCRE with high DNase, H3K4me3 and H3K27ac, and VEP annotates a promoter regulatory feature. The z-scores are maxima across biosamples, which is acknowledged. This is epigenomic context that fits a promoter element.

Proximity (0 kb from the TERT TSS) plus a literature statement that these mutations promote TERT expression. No eQTL, CRISPR or reporter data are cited here. This is indirect support, as the chain itself acknowledges.

GABPA expression of 15.5 TPM in glioblastoma lines and the active chromatin context make occupancy plausible, but the chromatin z-scores are not glioblastoma-specific. The DepMap common-essential result is correctly treated as non-lineage-specific. No glioblastoma occupancy data are cited.

Quotes support TERT promoter mutations being frequent in glioblastoma and melanoma and TERT loss triggering senescence in a melanoma context. They do not tie GABPA or this chain to the phenotype, as the chain concedes.

The ETS specificity is shared across the group, but ETS1 has only a CIS-BP-mapped model and is not a listed passing member. ETS1 is nominated purely on expression, so there is no ETS1-specific binding evidence. The literature on ETS site creation is generic.
The variant lies in an active promoter-like cCRE with strong DNase, H3K4me3 and H3K27ac signal. The cited cCRE data show this directly.
Only proximity and generic literature on mutations promoting TERT expression support this. Nothing is specific to ETS1, and no perturbation or QTL data are cited.

ETS1 expression of 61 TPM shows availability in glioblastoma lines, and the chain admits no occupancy data. The cited ChIP evidence (E16) is for GABPA, not ETS1, so it does not support ETS1 occupancy.
The quotes support TERT promoter mutations being common in melanoma and glioblastoma, but they say nothing about ETS1. This is general phenotype context only.

Four AP-2 models pass with ref-preferring sign and TFAP2A has its own model (z -28.06), but this is an in vitro binding prediction alone with a smaller effect than the ETS gain. There is no occupancy or perturbation evidence.
The cCRE is an active promoter, but no evidence shows AP-2 acts at this element, as the chain itself states. This is context only.

The literature mentions displacement of negative regulators but names no factor, and nothing cited connects AP-2 to TERT repression. Proximity and a generic mechanism are all that is offered, so this is speculative.
TFAP2A and TFAP2C are expressed in glioblastoma lines, so occupancy of the reference site is possible. There are no ChIP data and the cited evidence is expression only.
The quotes show TERT promoter mutations are common in glioblastoma and melanoma, but nothing links a loss of AP-2 binding to the phenotype.

G020 shows a strong alt-preferring effect and ETV6 has its own passing model (z 46.32), but this is a binding prediction alone. ETV6 is chosen by exclusion on expression, and its best model is not the group best. No occupancy data are cited.
The cCRE is an active promoter, but the chain concedes no evidence identifies ETV6 activity there. This is context only.
Only the gene proximity list is cited. Nothing supports ETV6 repression of TERT or dampening of its expression, and the claim of modulation is unsupported.

ETV6 expression of 5.65 TPM shows it is expressed in glioblastoma lines, so it is available. The claim about its limited influence relative to other ETS factors is an inference and is not shown by the evidence.
The cited rs2853669 cis data on TERT expression and survival do not mention ETV6, and the chain admits no evidence links the variability to it. Nothing bears on the claim.

A major molecular feature of melanoma is abnormal telomerase activation; this is most often caused by telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter mutations, which occur in 50-82% of cases and are the most common noncoding alteration in this cancer.
CDKN2A and CDK4 mutations act through UV-dependent and cell cycle disruption pathways, while BAP1, POT1, and TERT mutations are considered UV-independent.
The single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) rs2853669, also located in the TERT promoter, may influence telomerase activity, though its clinical relevance in GBM remains unclear.

Patients carrying the SNP and TPM on the same allele (C/C and T/C cis) had shorter overall survival than those carrying them on different alleles (T/T or T/C trans; 19 vs 25 months, p = 0.048), and TERT expression was also lower in this group (p = 0.038).
Additionally, loss of either USP10 or FOXM1 suppresses the expression of the downstream target Telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT), triggering cellular senescence.

TERT promoter (TERTp) mutations are among the most frequent molecular alterations in isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) wild-type glioblastoma (GBM), yet the molecular profiles and prognostic implications associated with TERTp status remain incompletely characterized.

PMID 38278800 (2024): The regulations of telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) in cancer.

Canonical TERTp mutations create de novo binding sites for ETS family transcription factors that induce favourable conditions for DNA damage formation by UV light, thus creating a hotspot effect but only after a first mutational hit.
Specifically, AURKB, via REST, is recruited to TERTp MUT by TRIM28.

These mutations promote TERT gene expression by multiple mechanisms, including the generation of novel binding sites for nuclear transcription factors, displacement of negative regulators from DNA G-quadruplexes, recruitment of epigenetic activators and disruption of long-range interactions between TERT locus and telomeres.
